title: Conjugate gradient and the step length
goal:
Implement the two numerical pieces of Appendix C that turn a gradient $g$ into a trust-region step.

- `conjugate_gradient(fvp, b, iters=10, tol=1e-10)` approximately solves $Ax = b$, where $A$ is the Fisher matrix. It must use only the function `fvp(v)`, which returns $Av$. Never form $A$. Start from $x = 0$, run at most `iters` iterations, and stop early when $r^\top r < \text{tol}$.
- `max_step_length(s, As, delta)` returns $\beta = \sqrt{2\delta / (s^\top A s)}$, the largest step along the search direction $s \approx A^{-1} g$ for which the quadratic model of the KL divergence stays at $\delta$. The caller passes `As`, the product $As$, because CG has already computed it.

The tests use the $2 \times 2$ system from the page and random positive-definite systems.
hints: Keep three vectors: the solution `x`, the residual `r = b - A x`, and the search direction `p`. Start with `x = 0`, `r = b`, and `p = r`.
One iteration: `alpha = (r @ r) / (p @ A p)`, then `x += alpha * p`, `r -= alpha * A p`, then `p = r_new + ((r_new @ r_new) / (r_old @ r_old)) * p`.
In exact arithmetic, CG solves an $n \times n$ system in at most $n$ iterations. If a test with 2 iterations on a $2 \times 2$ system fails, check the formula for the new direction `p`.
From $\tfrac12 \beta^2 s^\top A s = \delta$, solve for $\beta$. Check the factor of 2 and the square root.
